newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares rally to close before handover.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares rally to close before handover.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market ended up in a rebound on Friday ahead of the Hong Kong handover holiday, due to institutional buying in shares of firms expected to post good 1997 interim results, brokers said.
The B share index rallied 0.91 points or 0.63 percent to end at 144.72 after losses for four straight sessions. Turnover expanded to HK$106 million from Thursday's HK$67 million.

But the domestic A share market dipped 10.66 points or 2.32 percent to 449.42 as investors pulled out before the long holiday amid concerns that Beijing may introduce fresh anti-speculative measures in July, brokers said.
A share turnover reached 11.5 billion yuan, compared with 9.4 billion yuan on Thursday.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange has announced it will close on June 30 and July 1 to mark the handover and trading will resume on Wednesday July 2.
"Buying that was focused on counters expected to post strong 1997 interim earnings boosted the B share index," Cheng Li, a B share analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"The B share market have bottomed out just above the 140-point level, which should be a strong medium-term support," Cheng said.
Analysts said they expected most listed firms to report slightly better first-half results this year with the effect of last year's two interest rate cuts flowing through to the 1997 interim results.
"Interim results will be the main factor influencing the market next month, with the Hong Kong handover factor fading away," Ren Zhengwei, an analyst at Xiangcai Securities said.
Investors had expected handover euphoria to prevent Beijing from cracking down on the market but the fact has gone against their will.
"People have begun shifting attention to counters aided by talk of strong interim earnings," Song Bin, an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
But worries that Beijing may carry out new counter-speculation measures aimed at the A share market in July will cap share rises, analysts said.
"The performance of the post-handover B share market should largely depend on that of red-chips and H shares and the upcoming giant B share newcomer Bengang Steel," Song added.
Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd has ended its initial public offering of 460 million B shares for listing in Shenzhen in early July.

In the B share market, Chenming Paper, helped by investor optimism over its interim profits, surged HK$0.48 or 6.77 percent to HK$7.57 to be the sharpest gainer on Friday. It was also the most actively traded issue on volume of 4.2 million shares.
Second best performer Konka Group, one of China's biggest colour television makers in Shenzhen, powered HK$0.49 or 4.45 percent to HK$11.49 as volume reached 301,749 shares.

Century Plaza Hotel was the weakest performer in the A share market, slumping 0.76 yuan or 8.19 percent to 8.52 yuan on selling triggered by talk that the company's interim results would be poor, brokers said.
